elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that “Sparkling may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate.”

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The clause permits Sparkling to assign without consent “to a successor in a merger.”

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The clause permits Sparkling to assign without consent “to a successor in an ... acquisition.”

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The clause permits Sparkling to assign without consent “to a successor in a ... sale of substantially all assets.”

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) prohibits Garman from assigning the Agreement or its rights and obligations without the other party’s written consent, which in this Garman-specific sentence means Sparkling’s consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that “Sparkling's consent to an assignment by Garman shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause categorically states that “Garman may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Sparkling,” without a consent exception.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate as a result of Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that “Garman shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a change of control of Sparkling.”

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Sparkling may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice requirement applies to Sparkling’s permitted successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Garman receives no successor-assignment exception; Section (d) requires Sparkling’s written consent for Garman’s assignments.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice mechanism for Garman successor assignments and instead requires prior consent.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: The conformed Section (c) permits Sparkling to assign only as allowed by Section 20(d) or when authorized by Garman in writing, so other assignments require Garman’s written authorization.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) requires Sparkling’s written consent for Garman’s assignments and provides no broader exception.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard applies only to Sparkling’s consent to an assignment by Garman; no equivalent restriction applies to Garman’s authorization of a Sparkling assignment.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Sparkling’s consent to an assignment by Garman shall not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position, including each permitted Customer assignment category, the Vendor consent and reasonableness requirements, the absolute competitor bar, and the prohibition on termination following Customer change of control. The fallback is not independently satisfied because Vendor lacks a notice-only successor-assignment right, neither party has the required successor-assignment notice duties, and Garman’s consent to Sparkling’s other assignments is not subject to a reasonableness standard. The changes are confined to assignment-related language and a necessary conforming cross-reference, although “the other party” in the Garman-only restriction is less precise than naming Sparkling directly.
